mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the unemployment rate increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic demand, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where real GDP growth increases over two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% over two months signals a supply-side contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where industrial production decreases by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending is expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances where nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 300,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) both increase by more than 2% in a month, it signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and investment in housing are expected to boost corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both housing starts and real personal consumption expenditures increase by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and borrowing costs rise.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the federal funds rate is above 3% and the Consumer Price Index increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% in a month and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the same month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the unemployment rate decreases by more than 0.3% and nonfarm payrolls increase by more than 200,000 in a month.
